messages:
nate: Quick follow-up on the legacy-span normalizer work — found a few edge cases that change the tradeoffs.
maria: tl;dr what are the edge cases? :thinking:
nate: Two main ones:
- legacy spans sometimes have caller info in tags.caller vs attributes.caller_id
- some spans are compressed/stacked by the agent and we lose ordering metadata so dedupe logic breaks
kevin: ugh. are these happening frequently in prod traces or just in old SDKs?
nate: mostly older SDKs (v0.9.x) and a small percentage of mobile telemetry. It shows up when we try to canonicalize keys aggressively.
maria: can you paste an example of before/after normalization? that helps me reason about idempotency
nate: sure

```
// raw span from old SDK
{"trace_id":"t1","span_id":"s1","tags":{"caller":"svc-a"},"attrs":{"lat_ms":12}}

// normalized target
{"trace_id":"t1","span_id":"s1","service":"svc-a","lat_ms":12}
```

nate: Problem: if we run a normalizer at the edge and later run pipeline-level enrichment, we might double-apply transforms or map caller->service differently. also, some micro-batches re-order spans so dedupe by (trace_id, span_id) may drop valid updates.
maria: so two options: 1) make ingestion normalizer conservative (non-destructive, additive), 2) normalize in pipeline with a one-shot backfill job and stronger idempotency guarantees.
zara: option 1 keeps downstream consumers stable (no schema churn) but means we carry multiple alias keys for longer => cost + cardinality impact.
kevin: option 2 centralizes logic and lets us backfill, but requires a migration job and a freeze window for consumers to adopt new field names. Also more complex rollback.
ingest-bot: Deploy note: ingestion changes require config rollout across edge fleet; estimated 2-4 hours for canary then global.
maria: proposal: do a conservative edge shim that copies aliases to canonical fields without removing old keys. Add a pipeline dedupe+canonicalizer that can collapse aliases in a controlled migration window. Steps:
1) edge shim (non-destructive): copy tags.caller -> service if missing.
2) pipeline canonicalizer (idempotent): always prefer canonical service field, but merge if only alias present.
3) one-time backfill job to clean historical data for billing/agg correctness.
4) add invariant tests and a probe metric: span_normalizer_applied{stage=edge|pipeline}

nate: +1. that reduces rollback blast radius.
kevin: timeline/owners?
maria: I'll prototype the edge shim and a tiny invariant testset (ETA 3d).
kevin: I'll scope the backfill and migration window with analytics (ETA 1w).
zara: I'll own the probe metrics and add dashboards; will add an alert if normalized cardinality jumps >10%.
maria: also: we should add a small sample to retention pipeline so we can validate before full backfill. maybe 1% sample of historical traces.
kevin: agree. also need to document the exact field mappings in a short RFC (schema-v2 migration). I'll draft the RFC after prototype.
nate: can we add a quick lint rule so future SDKs don't reintroduce 'caller' vs 'caller_id' inconsistencies?
maria: yes, add an ingest lint check that flags unknown caller aliases during canary.
zara: putting owners: maria (edge shim + tests), kevin (backfill + migration plan), zara (metrics + alerts), nate (schema review + rollback plan).
kevin: ok will create a Kanban card and milestone.
maria: created a branch: feat/edge-span-shim and pushed small PR with unit tests. link: https://git.local/r/edge-span-shim
nate: awesome — let's sync tomorrow 09:30 for a short demo. :eyes:
maria: sounds good. thanks all!
